newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to probe bank consolidation irregularities.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to probe bank consolidation irregularities.

text.p: Hungary's Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy will set up a committee to investigate alleged irregularities during the bank consolidation programme of the early 1990s, the Ministry said in a statement on Thursday.
The committee has to finish its work in 30 days.

Hungary's previous government spent over 300 billion forints between 1992 and 1994 for bailing out banks troubled by bad debts. The State Audit Office (ASZ) said in a report published on Wednesday that, during the programme, the state and the banks concluded contracts unfavourable for the state budget.

The ASZ requested the banks involved and the Finance Ministry to find the persons responsible for the alleged irregularities and also asked the Chief Prosecutor's Office to investigate if the irregularities breached criminal law.

The Finance Ministry said in the statement it did not agree with many points in the ASZ report. The banks affected by the ASZ's allegations include Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB), Hungary's fifth largest bank, which the state plans to privatise this year.

MHB said in a separate statement that its management has been replaced since the period covered by the ASZ report, but the bank will launch internal investigations to find out staff who might have been responsible for the alleged irregularities. ASZ said the irregularities which happened at the MHB cost the state budget an extra 200 million forints.
